title: genderHeart – A Prospective Observational Study of Sex-Specific Secondary Prevention and Follow-Up Care After Acute Coronary Syndrome
summary:
The genderHeart study investigates whether changes in voice can provide early indications of an increased risk of recurrent cardiovascular events following an acute coronary syndrome (e.g., a heart attack). The study aims to determine whether combining voice analysis with other health data collected during the study, using artificial intelligence, can improve the assessment of an individual's cardiovascular risk.

Patients following an acute coronary syndrome will be monitored over a period of six months. In addition to regular follow-up visits, various parameters will be assessed, including blood pressure, heart rate, blood values, and hormone levels. Participants will also complete questionnaires on their health status and quality of life. Furthermore, they will regularly record voice samples using a smartphone app. These recordings will be digitally analyzed to identify potential changes in voice over time. An additional telephone follow-up will take place after one year.

Particular attention will be paid to potential differences between women and men. The aim is to investigate whether combining these different types of information can improve the assessment of changes in health status and the risk of further cardiovascular events.

In the long term, the findings are intended to contribute to more personalized cardiovascular follow-up care after a heart attack or other acute coronary syndrome, taking into account the specific needs of women and men. The digital procedures used in the study are exclusively for research purposes and do not make independent medical decisions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Adult patients following acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or type 1 myocardial infarction (MI).
•	Clinically stable and able to use the TEDIAS assistance station and the app.
•	 Capacity to provide informed consent for study participation and continuous data collection (vital signs, voice biomarkers, laboratory values, and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs)).
•	Willingness to attend the scheduled study visits, participate in digital data collection, and complete follow-up over several months.
•	Availability of a smartphone for app use.
Exclusion criteria:
•	Severe cognitive impairment, dementia, or significant language barriers that prevent independent use of the app or assistance station.
•	Speech or hearing impairments, as well as severe pulmonary diseases that significantly interfere with voice analysis.
•	Advanced malignancy with an expected life expectancy of less than one year.
•	Infectious diseases (e.g., hepatitis, HIV).
•	Acute severe comorbidities that significantly impair or prevent follow-up or participation in the monitoring procedures.
